solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parent, with child, is stone dresser

parts.note: MA is an informal word for a mother
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A family pair turns out to work as a craftsman dressing stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who cuts and dresses blocks of stone for building.

clue.text: Small creature's power spoken about

indicators.note: spoken about signals that the word for power is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: might means strength or power

explanation.surface: A remark on how a tiny animal's strength gets talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a tiny arachnid, a byword for a very small creature.

clue.text: Remain in street? Indeed

parts.note: AY (aye) is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to stay put on the street and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is a direct synonym of to remain in place.

clue.text: Food item held by parvenu — trim entryist

indicators.note: held by says the answer is contained within the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A social climber who has slimmed down is described as an infiltrator holding food.
explanation.walkthrough: An entryist is someone who joins an organisation in order to subvert it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishing matter, anything that feeds a body, so a food item fits.

clue.text: Do better than Spurs, say, almost unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out in an unforeseen order, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word say is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A football commentator predicts that Tottenham Hotspur nearly outdid expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. 'almost' trims SAY to SA; 'unexpectedly' shuffles SPURS plus SA.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to exceed or outdo them, the same as doing better.

clue.text: County certain to welcome king over year

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above, before, the letter for year
to welcome means one word takes another in, so the letter for king goes inside the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A county is sure to receive the monarch for a year-long visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrey is a county in south-east England, just south of London.

clue.text: Friend regularly embarrassed-looking?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word Friend, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A pal who often seems to be blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed turns red in the face, so the colour describes an embarrassed look.

clue.text: Separately priced — a vehicle coming in behind time

indicators.note: coming in means the vehicle's word enters the middle of the word for behind time

parts.note: late means behind time
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car arriving late gets an itemised bill.
explanation.definitionFit: On a menu, à la carte dishes are each priced individually rather than as a set meal.

clue.text: More sensible to include chapter referring to wine

indicators.note: to include means the word for more sensible takes the letter for chapter inside it

parts.note: saner means more sensible
RE means concerning or referring to, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Advice to be more prudent by adding a chapter about wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancerre is a white wine from the Loire valley in France, an example of a wine.

clue.text: One raising glass — it's for Browning?

definitions.meaning: someone proposing a health at a party lifts a glass
a kitchen gadget that browns bread; Browning also suggests the poet Robert Browning

explanation.surface: A guest raises a glass to honour the poet Browning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person proposing a toast and the appliance that toasts bread share the name.

clue.text: Duke drops pipe

parts.note: rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A nobleman abandons his tobacco pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb but is a noun, raindrops.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe or channel carrying away waste water.

clue.text: Route to safety? Cook safe recipe

indicators.note: to cook something up is to fiddle or rearrange it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to follow a foolproof recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is a staircase or exit by which people leave a burning building safely.

clue.text: Top performer makes commitment to join group including Leo?

parts.note: a star is a leading performer
someone who signs puts their name to an agreement

explanation.surface: A celebrity signs up with a band featuring someone called Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve zodiac divisions known collectively by this name, so it is a member example.

clue.text: In all likelihood supporting Bishop in skilful way

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ably means in a skilful way

explanation.surface: Backing a bishop is likely the clever course.
explanation.definitionFit: Probably is an adverb meaning very likely, matching the phrase about likelihood.

clue.text: One moving fast from Dinant, eloper

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone running off to marry flees from Dinant, a town in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift-running hoofed animal, one that moves fast.

clue.text: One making regular payments, torn, I hesitate to say

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
ER is the sound a hesitating speaker makes

explanation.surface: A tenant in two minds hesitantly confesses to struggling with the payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A renter is a tenant who pays a landlord rent at regular intervals.

clue.text: Seaman repeatedly seen as fearsome person

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word for seaman appears twice in a row

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor keeps getting labelled as a terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a violent-tempered or formidable person, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Daughter altering route for longer one?

indicators.note: altering means the letters of route are changed around

explanation.surface: A daughter changes the planned route to take a longer one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'route' does double duty in the surface but is only the fodder; 'longer one?' alone defines, 'one' standing for a route.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout way that takes longer than the direct road.

clue.text: Small fliers, greenest distributed, in outskirts of Boulogne

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the outer pair
outskirts of means the first and last letters of Boulogne
distributed means the letters of greenest are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Some birds spread around the green edges of a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' makes RENTGEES; 'Small fliers' is fair because the brent is one of the smallest geese, despite the surface suggesting a French scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Brent geese are small dark geese, so they are an example of birds that fly.

clue.text: Wintry weather in South at present time

parts.note: now means the present time

explanation.surface: A forecast of cold conditions in southern parts right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is the frozen precipitation typical of winter weather.

clue.text: Mark film award, overlooking nothing

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the letter for nothing is dropped

parts.note: an Oscar is the Academy Award for films
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An Oscar is marked as not being given to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: It sweeps up? Right, in successful period

indicators.note: in means the letter for right goes within the word for a successful period

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic success

explanation.surface: Someone sweeping up agrees it is a time of prosperity.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a brush on a long handle used for sweeping floors.

clue.text: Slander at first, most unfair detraction

indicators.note: at first means taking the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Defamation is described as, at first, a thoroughly unjust belittling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud stands for scandalous accusations, as in mud-slinging, so it means slander.

clue.text: Like some food products in cargo, exotic

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange or foreign, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some foods arrive as unusual imports in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic food is produced without synthetic chemicals, a label applied to many products.

clue.text: He concedes fielder needs new start

indicators.note: needs new start means the first letter of fielder is swapped for a different one

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder admits defeat and wants a fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the new first letter: the definition fixes it, swapping F for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or concede, so one who yields concedes.

clue.text: One scattering seeds ultimately manages to follow the supervisor

indicators.note: ultimately means taking the final letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: A gardener spreading seed finally manages to keep up with the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A sower is someone who scatters seed over the ground for planting.
